report_meta.subtitle: Eastern Cape Regional Performance

sections.text: Game Jeffery's Bay is the standout concern this month -- 81.25% on-time, nearly double the regional late rate and the single worst-performing store across both banners. Unlike Makro, where courier SLA non-adherence dominates, Game's biggest late-order driver is Late Driver Assignment (25%), almost entirely Customer Request Date Changes, pointing to a promise-management issue rather than a courier failure. Cancellations are concentrated: Game Vincent East London accounts for 79% of the region's R14,544.28 cancelled value, but that's a single R10,433.91 fridge order, not a broad pattern -- Greenacres' higher-frequency, lower-value pattern is the more systemic issue to watch.

executive_facts.statement: Late Driver Assignment (25% of the region's 9 late orders in that category) being almost entirely Customer Request Date Changes suggests a promise-management or communication issue, not a courier capacity failure -- the fix here is different from Makro's courier-escalation lever.

Beacon Bay's CSAT score of 70% is a standalone outlier -- every other Game store scores 87% or higher, and Beacon Bay's own delivery metrics don't explain the gap, pointing to an in-store or service experience issue distinct from delivery timing.

Greenacres is the weakest store on Pick SLA (90.13%) despite not standing out badly on OTD -- worth checking whether pick delays there are being absorbed elsewhere in the chain rather than surfacing as late orders yet.

Vincent East London's R11,506.76 in cancelled value is 79% of the region's total, but confirming whether the R10,433.91 fridge cancellation within it is a one-off stock/logistics failure matters more than treating it as a trend -- Greenacres' 24-order, 62-unit pattern is the more systemic issue to address separately.

sections.text: Prioritise Game Jeffery's Bay for OTD intervention and confirm the Vincent East London fridge cancellation is a one-off before treating cancellations as a trend -- Greenacres' order-frequency pattern is the real systemic risk there.

provenance.extraction_notes: One-page condensed view of Part B (Game) of the Eastern Cape monthly regional report. Cancelled-value-by-store breakdown reconciles exactly to the stated region total (R14,544.28 Ex VAT). The source also gives a General Merchandise (80%) vs Food (20%) division split of cancelled value, but only as rounded approximate figures (R11.7k / R2.9k) that don't sum precisely to the exact region total -- it was left out of this one-pager rather than presented as a reconciling breakdown it isn't. Late Order Deep Dive root cause is the Game-wide regional total (36 orders), not store-specific -- the source states a Jeffery's Bay-only extract has not yet been supplied, and this report preserves that caveat. Recommended Focus Areas from the source (5 items) were condensed to fit a one-page format.
